doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: The World's Greatest Jazz Band, Dick Gibson and Cliff Leeman
summary: Dick Gibson named the band; Rosengarden played in it after Cliff Leeman and tells of Haggart's 'Fog'.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who named “The World’s Greatest Jazz Band?”
So it wasn’t one of the players.

No. Dick Gibson was, is still alive, out in Denver. An impresario. I mean he was a businessman who did very well and he loved Hag and he loved Yank Lawson. Yank was quite a drinker in those days. And so Yank would mumble a lot, and Hag was just Mount Pleasant. And I played in that band at various times. Cliff Leeman was the first drummer. And Cliff did a wonderful job for that band, much better than I did. I imitated him. I did my mimicking. I imitated what he did. But he meant it. And I enjoyed playing with that band because it was good players. Of course I love playing with Hag anyway, he’s such a good player. Such a good musician. I don’t think it’s telling tales out of school, we’d call him “The Fog.“ I mean he kind of goes away. You know, you’ll see him and talk to him and all of a sudden you know he just left, he just left. “Come back!” He comes back. And he laughs at himself about it too. He always looks so serene when he goes away like that, I think to myself, gee I wish I could do that.
